newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CRUYFF UNIMPRESSED BY ROBSON'S BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUYFF UNIMPRESSED BY ROBSON'S BARCELONA.

text.p: Former Barcelona coach Johan Cruyff is unimpressed by the work done so far by his successor in the post, ex-England manager Bobby Robson.
"Frankly, they're playing badly," said Cruyff in remarks published in the Spanish sports daily Marca on Wednesday.
Neverthless the Dutchman recognises that over time Robson's new-look Barcelona, who are top of the league after five games, could improve.

"It's a new team that needs time to fit together...it would be absurd if they were to play well after so little time," said Cruyff, who is a season-ticket holder at the club and is given a hero's reception by fans at home games.
But Cruyff also had harsh words for club president Jose Luis Nunez over the possible transfer of defender Miguel Angel Nadal to English champions Manchester United.

"I'm not sure what's going to happen...but each time I read something about it in the papers it makes me sick," said Cruyff, who is considering legal action for slander over remarks made by Nunez in a press conference the day after he was sacked.
Cruyff has already brought two cases against the club in relation to earnings and bonuses lost when his eight years at Barcelona came to an end in May.
The first case awarded the Dutchman 30 million pesetas ($234,000), but both sides have subsequently appealed the decision.
Cruyff said he still hadn't considered whether he would coach another Spanish side.
